reason:
The worker's 2.0.16 recovery holds up under my read-only review of the actual diff and sources. All 110 unsafe annotations came from 5 generic templates in types/fulu.bend, instantiated for 22 element types. They were replaced with ordinary per-type definitions (`NodeN.seq_*`) that do the same work. Every self-call in them recurses on a smaller part of its input, so they terminate. The three adapter proof files were regenerated. Their changes are pure renames: the lemma statements and proof steps are the same, now naming the new functions. END_TO_END.bend is not in the diff. Its five public laws are unchanged and universally quantified over the real API.

The new loader compiles each imported .bend module with the pinned bend binary and re-exports the compiled output unchanged. The tests are not in the diff. Frozen acceptance (automation/acceptance.py) passed under 2.0.16: both proof roots check with zero unsafe annotations, the runtime tests pass, and 5440 of 5440 SSZ cases pass. The runner says eligible_for_completion=true. The independent auditor approved with only low-severity documentation findings.
evidence: Runner validation: acceptance.py rc=0 after 2325s; stdout ends 'SSZ: 5440 passed, 0 failed, 5440 inventoried' then END_TO_END.bend 'All terms check.'. acceptance.py:25 rejects any nonzero unsafe count or @unsafe text, and PROOF.bend passed the same check at line 51.

diff.patch lines 60314+: the generic to_items_go/to_items/from_step/from_items_go/from_items templates (~A) are replaced by NodeN.seq_to_go/seq_to/seq_step/seq_from_go/seq_from. The bodies are the same and recursion is on the list or Items tail.

diff.patch lines 1385+ (proofs/fulu_adapter_inverse.bend): the law statements are the same except that the new names replace the template calls. The proof terms and the induction structure are unchanged.

tools/unsafe-2.0.16: INVENTORY.md lists all 110 instances (5 templates x 22 types). template_count.bend gives '2 unsafe annotations' and mono.bend gives 'All terms check.' (output.txt). This is the checker's intended treatment of templates, not a kernel defect.
Grep for '(~', ', ~', '@unsafe' and 'axiom' across *.bend matches only the reproducer tools/unsafe-2.0.16/template_count.bend.

END_TO_END.bend is not in the diff. serialize_correct (line 75), deserialize_correct (106), deserialize_rejection_correct (147), hash_tree_root_correct (181) and fulu_types_correct (301) are stated over API.serialize/deserialize/hash_tree_root and Fulu.Name, and specified with Legal/Encoding/Decoding/Roots from spec/*.
spec/*.bend imports only Base, ./spec, the neutral ../types/{schema,primitive,byte_alias,list_alias}.bend and ../vendor/bend_sha256/fips.bend. None imports src/ or proofs/.

tools/bend_loader.ts checks the toolchain.json hashes, runs pinned `bend page.html -o out`, requires exit 0 and exactly one chunk, and re-exports the compiled module. The cache key covers the toolchain, every workspace .bend file and the entry file.

tools/run_runtime_tests.py requires explicit test files and checks the pinned hashes. It fails on a bun nonzero exit, zero tests, any fail or error, a file-count mismatch, or loader/compile error text.
tools/spectests.py diff: only PRELOAD changes to the local loader, plus version and hash provenance fields. The case logic and expected_outputs_sent_to_backend=False are unchanged.
The diff contains no tests/ files, so tests/sha256.test.ts and tests/new/*.test.ts are unchanged. No protected paths are modified.

criteria.evidence: types/fulu.bend keeps every Node/Name definition and its Spec.SchemaN link. The change only makes the sequence helpers monomorphic. fulu_types_correct at END_TO_END.bend:301 still quantifies over all Fulu.Name, and the 5440 static and generic cases pass.

src/ssz.bend is unchanged. The per-type seq helpers compute exactly what the template instances computed. Runtime tests and all 5440 official cases pass through modules compiled by the pinned 2.0.16 compiler (tools/bend_loader.ts).
spec/*.bend is unchanged and does not import src/ or proofs/, only the neutral types/ and vendor FIPS. The Legal/Encoding/Decoding/Roots relations it defines are used by the END_TO_END laws.

The five END_TO_END laws are unchanged and universal over schema/value/bytes/Name. The adapter proofs were regenerated with the same statements, now naming the new per-type helpers. PROOF.bend and END_TO_END.bend give 'All terms check.' with zero unsafe annotations under pinned 2.0.16 in frozen acceptance.

HASH_PROOF.bend, src/sha256.bend and vendor/bend_sha256 are protected and not in the diff. The spec imports vendor/bend_sha256/fips.bend. PROOF.bend checks cleanly and tests/sha256.test.ts passes in runtime acceptance.

Frozen acceptance: 5440 passed, 0 failed, 5440 inventoried, and every row status is 'passed', matching cases.json. Backend nonzero exits and timeouts still count as failures, and expected outputs are not sent to the backend.

No @unsafe, axiom or template (~) remains outside the reproducer. The checker reports zero unsafe annotations. The compiler, loader, Bun and transport are documented as trusted and outside the proofs in PROOF_STATUS.md. The toolchain hashes are pinned and checked in the loader, the runner and acceptance.

risks: The loader depends on the 2.0.16 page-bundler behaviour (`bend page.html -o dir`). This is pinned by hash but would need re-verification on any toolchain change.

The standalone spectest report tools/validation-bend-2.0.16-official-29a6….json predates the widening of the loader cache key to vendor/*.bend and is superseded by the acceptance report. This is low-severity documentation.
The top-level VALIDATION.json 'iteration': 11 could be confused with the recovery run. This is low severity.
I did not re-run the checker or the tests myself (read-only). I rely on the runner's frozen acceptance execution together with my own source and diff inspection.
The runtime is limited: Nat is capped at 2^48-1, and memory and time are bounded. Failures from these limits count as failures, never as rejections.
